issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the Ride attribute: the UML in problem_statement.md declares Ride with an attribute named 'abbreviation' (type char), but the solution implementation (src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java) declares the corresponding field as 'shortName' (char) and provides the getter getShortName(). Students are instructed to provide getters for all UML attributes and to follow the UML constructor parameter order, so this mismatch (abbreviation vs shortName / getAbbreviation() vs getShortName()) can confuse them about the expected field name, constructor parameter name, and getter name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Either update the solution/template to use the name 'abbreviation' for the Ride field and provide getAbbreviation() (and adjust constructor parameter names and subclass constructor calls accordingly), or update the UML/problem statement to use 'shortName' and document the getter getShortName(). Ensure tests and instructions reference the chosen identifier so students implement the expected field and getter.
